tasks.title: Make `mo issue create` accept file-backed bodies and fail clearly
tasks.description: Update the create command so issue bodies can come from literal text, curl-style `@file`, explicit `--body-file`, or `--body -` stdin input before the request is sent to the API. This same task should normalize create priority case-insensitively, exit with code 1 on invalid user input or body-ingestion failures, and add the conditional post-create `mo issue start` tip when the returned issue is still idle.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo issue create "Title" --body @file.md` reads the file contents as the created issue body
`mo issue create "Title" --body-file file.md` reads the file contents as the created issue body
`mo issue create "Title" --body -` reads the full body from stdin without requiring shell escaping
`mo issue create -p P2` is accepted and stored the same as `-p p2`
Missing files, invalid `--body`/`--body-file` combinations, invalid priority, and other create-argument validation failures print a clear error and exit with code 1

Successful creation prints `Created issue #N: <title>` plus priority, and prints `Tip: Run 'mo issue start <number>' to begin processing` only when the created issue is still in a startable backlog or draft state
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Resolve body sources at the CLI boundary and keep the API payload shape as plain `body?: string`.

tasks.title: Extend update and issue write APIs to share the new body and priority contract
tasks.description: Apply the same body-resolution behavior to `mo issue update --body` so update supports literal text, `@file`, and `-` stdin while preserving plain-string compatibility. In the same outcome, make the create and update API write paths accept case-insensitive priority values so CLI and direct HTTP clients follow one contract for issue writes.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo issue update <number> --body @file.md` reads the file contents as the updated issue body
`mo issue update <number> --body -` reads the full body from stdin as the updated issue body
A literal `--body` value that does not start with `@` and is not `-` still behaves as a direct string body
Unreadable files, stdin read failures, invalid priority, and other touched update validation failures print a clear error and exit with code 1
`POST /issues` and `PATCH /issues/:id` accept `P0`-`P4` and normalize them the same as lowercase values
API invalid-priority responses remain 400-class validation failures rather than silently accepting bad input
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Prefer a shared normalization path so create and update do not drift again. `--body-file` is only required on create for this change.

tasks.title: Normalize list priority filtering across CLI and API
tasks.description: Make issue list filtering accept uppercase and lowercase priority input consistently from the CLI through the HTTP API. This task should use the same normalization rules as create and update, while ensuring invalid list filters fail explicitly instead of returning a misleading successful command result.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo issue list -p P1` filters issues the same way as `mo issue list -p p1`
The API list endpoint accepts uppercase priority filters and returns the same filtered results as lowercase input
Invalid list priority input prints a clear CLI validation error and exits with code 1
The CLI and API use one consistent normalization rule for all touched issue priority inputs rather than separate case-handling behavior
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/src/cli/commands/issue.ts, packages/cli/src/api/issues.ts, and shared priority normalization helpers
tasks.notes: This task depends on the shared write-path normalization introduced for create/update and extends it to list filtering.

tasks.title: Add focused regression coverage for body sources, priority normalization, exits, and success guidance
tasks.description: Add or update automated coverage so the new issue-authoring contract is locked in across CLI and API boundaries. Cover file and stdin body ingestion, missing-file and invalid-priority failures, case-insensitive create/update/list priority behavior, non-zero exit codes for touched CLI validation paths, and conditional start-tip rendering on create success.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover create body input via `@file`, `--body-file`, and stdin
Tests cover update body input via `@file` and stdin plus the preserved literal-string body path
Tests cover missing-file and invalid-priority failures, including non-zero CLI exit behavior for touched issue commands
Tests cover case-insensitive priority handling in CLI create, update, and list flows as well as API create, update, and list handlers
Tests cover that the create success tip appears only for startable issue states and is omitted otherwise
Relevant CLI and API test suites pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.output: packages/cli/tests/ and any touched issue CLI/API regression test files
tasks.notes: Prefer focused regression tests near the existing issue command and API coverage rather than broad new test infrastructure.

tasks.title: Update Mohist skill guidance for long issue bodies
tasks.description: Revise the shared `mohist` skill documentation so agents and users are guided toward file-backed or piped issue body input instead of shell-escaped long strings. The guidance should recommend `--body @file` as the default long-body workflow, mention `--body -` for pipelines, and keep heredoc or command substitution as fallback compatibility patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: `.agents/skills/mohist/SKILL.md` recommends `mo issue create --body @file.md` for long Markdown issue bodies
The skill guidance documents `--body -` as the pipe-oriented stdin workflow
The guidance no longer relies on warning users away from long bodies because of shell quoting limitations alone
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Keep the documentation aligned with the implemented CLI contract so agents stop recommending shell-escaping workarounds as the primary path.
